newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end virtually flat amid options expiry.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end virtually flat amid options expiry.

text.p: Brazil shares see-sawed to end virtually flat in heavy trading amid options settlements whose results failed to surprise the market, traders said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares ended up a slight eight points at 67,989 points. Turnover was 1.77 billion reais ($1.73 billion).

Investors exercised bellwether Telebras options at a strike price of 80 reais. Telebras preferred shares dropped 0.36 percent to close at 82.40 reais, after fluctuating between 82 and 83.50 reais during the session.

Traders expect the bourse to have a technical correction Tuesday and investors are likely to take moderate profits. They said developments on a possible congressional vote on proposed alterations to the government's civil service bill might weigh on prices tomorrow.

In addition, they will be eyeing a National Prizatization Council meeting scheduled to begin Tuesday at 10 a.m. (8 a.m. EDT) 1200 GMT. The council will discuss the privatization of ports and a proposal to include federal power generating firm to begin late next year.
Eletrobras preferred shares closed at 334 reais, down 1.47 percent on a technical correction, traders said.
Among big winners, Vale do Rio Doce preferred shares rose 0.95 percent to end at 21.20 reais.
Oil monopoly Petrobras preferred shares continued rallying today, closing at 136 reais, up 3.08 percent.
